You've got your MCP connected but what's next? What does it take to turn an MCP connection into a working application?
Join speakers from Elastic, Arcade.dev, and Temporal for a developer meetup exploring three pieces of that puzzle: connecting agents to data, governing their access, and bringing tools together into workflows.

Matt Ryan: Principal PM, Elastic — A look at Elastic’s new global MCP endpoint and what it enables for developers.

Bring your questions and the challenges you’re working on.

event.description:
About the Event
Kittu Kolluri has sat on both sides of the table more times than almost anyone in the Valley. He started as an engineer at Silicon Graphics, co-founded Healtheon (which became WebMD), then founded and ran Neoteris until NetScreen acquired it, and later led Juniper’s security business. He spent the next eleven years as a General Partner at NEA, where he was an early backer of Box, Robinhood, and The Climate Corporation.
In 2017 he left NEA to start Neotribe Ventures, a much smaller, earlier-stage firm that he describes as next generation but old fashioned. Neotribe backs founders working on hard technical problems in applied AI, security, energy, and the life sciences, and stays with them well past the first check through its Ignite growth fund.
Murali Chirala of FalconX Ventures will lead the conversation. Expect him to push on the questions founders actually want answered: how Kittu decides a technology is real before the market agrees, what made him double down on companies like BillionToOne all the way to its IPO, and what he’s seen kill otherwise promising startups from the inside.
Featured Speakers
Kittu Kolluri – Founder & Managing Director, Neotribe Ventures
Kittu founded Neotribe Ventures in 2017 to invest in breakthrough technologies at the seed and Series A stage. The firm has since raised multiple funds, including a $216 million second fund and the $90 million Ignite Fund, which follows on into portfolio companies at Series B and beyond. Its portfolio includes BillionToOne, Energy Vault, Fortanix, ThirdAI, and Hakimo.
Before Neotribe, Kittu spent eleven years as a General Partner at NEA, backing more than four dozen companies and serving on many of their boards. Earlier, he was EVP and GM of the Security Products Group at Juniper Networks, a role that followed NetScreen’s acquisition of Neoteris, the company he founded and led as CEO. He was also a co-founder of Healtheon/WebMD and began his career as an engineer at Silicon Graphics. He trained as a mechanical engineer at IIT Madras before moving into computer science at SUNY Buffalo.
Murali Chirala – Managing Partner, FalconX Ventures
Murali invests in early-stage companies and works closely with founders on growth and fundraising. He was the founding architect of India’s Aadhaar financial inclusion and payments platform, one of the largest fintech systems ever deployed, and now backs startups working on payments, fraud, compliance, security, and enterprise infrastructure. At Venture Dock he helps founders figure out what actually builds investor conviction and what just sounds good in a deck.
Agenda
2:00 – 2:30 PM Doors open, coffee & networking2:30 – 3:15 PM Fireside chat: Kittu Kolluri with Murali Chirala3:15 – 3:30 PM Open Q&A3:30 – 4:00 PM Members-only small group session with Kittu (by invitation)
About Build From The Dock
Build From The Dock is Venture Dock’s weekly founder experience, designed to create real connections between ambitious builders, investors, operators, and ecosystem leaders.
Unlike traditional networking events, BFTD focuses on high-value conversations where founders can engage directly with speakers and each other.
Whether you’re building an AI startup, scaling a company, raising capital, or exploring what’s next in technology, this is a space designed for meaningful relationships and actionable insights.
What Venture Dock Offers Founders
Beyond weekly sessions like this one, Venture Dock is built to be a real part of how founders operate day to day:
Investor introductions
Curated programming: roundtables, fireside chats, and working sessions with operators who’ve built and scaled before
Peer network: direct access to other founders building alongside you, for the honest conversations you can’t have with investors
Visibility with visiting delegations: opportunities to meet founders and ecosystem leaders coming through Silicon Valley from other markets
Ecosystem support: hiring, fundraising, and go-to-market help pulled from the community itself, not a generic playbook
What is Venture Dock
Venture Dock is a founder-first community and fund connecting startups with investors, operators, mentors, and strategic partners. Members get access to sessions like the one closing out this afternoon, where a smaller group sits down with the speaker after the main event.
If you’ve been coming to events and want deeper access, you can apply to join the community here: https://venturedock.fillout.com/t/gHcUcf7Tz8usAbout

event.description:
The first SF × MIT hack day is on energy. Sundai Club builds at MIT, we build at AGI House SF.
Guests from Stanford Energy Club.
Expect to hack on compute energy infrastructure and grid capacity forecasting.
A battery chemistry that lasts 20% longer or a grid model that predicts a failure an hour earlier is worth real money, and a lot of it can be tested in simulation before anyone touches hardware. We want agents that do that testing and get better at it each run.
Tracks for Nov 8
Edge Compute Management: Identify suitable sites, assess grid capacity, manage loads, and aggregate distributed compute to make it grid-friendly.
Materials for energy: search for battery, catalyst and solar materials with simulation in the loop.
Grid and fusion: forecasting, control and plasma simulation, wherever an agent can propose something and a model can check it.
Schedule
10:00 doors, coffee, intro
10:30  team formation
1:00 lunch
6:30 demos
7:30 done
Spots are limited and we approve applications on a rolling basis.
Who's behind it
AGI House SF is a hacker house on St. Germain Ave where researchers and founders meet to build on the frontier. We run hackathons, salons and dinners most weeks.
Sundai.club is the largest AI hacker community born out of Harvard & MIT that shipped more than 130+ hackathons back-to-back in the last 2.5 years - one for every sunday without stopping. 1000+ projects, with many funded by VCs, YC, etc.
RSIhouse.ai - a weekly open neutral space for hacks and dinners exclusively for recursive self improvement. We touch on topics of post-training, evals, harness engineering, self-play and swarm intelligence. Every week we explore the limits of RSI.
Autolab.ai is building infrastructure for the RSI. Starting with the evals, Autolab enables fully autonomous continual learning and ownership of your own enterprise AI models that get better with every API call you make.
Superradiant is a research lab building self-improving agents who are bringing the rapid advances in mathematics to the sciences.  The name comes from superradiance, the quantum effect where emitters that fall into phase radiate together and the light grows with N² instead of N. Their founders, Micah Stubbs and Alejandro Zarzuelo Urdiales, put this series together.Stanford Energy Club is Stanford’s premier student-led energy organization. The club hosts industry talks, networking events, and hands-on projects throughout the year, and recently organized Stanford Climate Week, featuring 70+ events in a single week.

The conversation will explore the rapidly evolving intersection of AI, healthcare, and AI for science. We’ll discuss how Artificial Intelligence is transforming healthcare delivery and clinical decision-making, and scientific innovation.
The session will bring together students, researchers, founders, investors, and industry leaders interested in the future of healthcare and AI.
About David Rhew:
Dr. David C. Rhew is the Global Chief Medical Officer (CMO) & VP of Healthcare for Microsoft. He is Adjunct Professor at Stanford University; holds six U.S. technology patents that enable authoring, mapping, and integration of clinical decision support into electronic health records; and has been recognized as one of the 50 most influential clinician executives by Modern Healthcare.
Dr. Rhew received his Bachelors of Science degrees in computer science and cellular molecular biology from University of Michigan. He received his MD degree from Northwestern University and completed internal medicine residency at Cedars-Sinai Medical Center. He completed fellowships in health services research at Cedars-Sinai and infectious diseases at the University of California, Los Angeles.
He has served as CMO and VP for Samsung; SVP and CMO at Zynx Health Incorporated; clinician/researcher at the VA Greater Los Angeles Healthcare System and RAND; and Associate Clinical Professor of Medicine at UCLA. Dr. Rhew has served on the National Quality Forum’s Executive Committee for Consensus Standards and Approval, Chaired the Consumer Technology Association Health Technology Board, and sits on the Governing Committee for NESTcc (National Evaluation System for health Technology coordinating center), the medical device advisory group for the FDA, CMS, and NIH.

After Tokens
The AI Economy Infrastructure Conference
What happens after the model call?
Tokens tell you what the model consumed. They don't tell you what a customer can use, when an agent should stop, or how a contract becomes a limit in your code.
After Tokens is about the infrastructure that answers those questions: metering, credits, entitlements, pricing, billing, and the systems that keep them in sync.
If you've had to meter an agent run, figure out what breaks when you move from tokens to credits, or check entitlements without slowing down the request, this day is for you.
One day, in person, in San Francisco: technical talks, architecture breakdowns, and lessons from systems running in production, aimed at the people who write the code.
Topics
Metering and usage data
Credits, limits, and entitlements
Pricing infrastructure
Billing and contracts
AI cost control
Agent economics
Usage systems at scale
Moving beyond token pricing
Who it's for
Engineers building AI products and the systems behind them: backend, platform, and AI infrastructure teams, technical founders, and engineering leaders.
When and where
When: Tuesday, November 10, 2026, 8:00 AM to 5:00 PM PT
Where: Terra, Rincon Hill / SoMa, San Francisco, a short walk from Embarcadero BART and the Salesforce Transit Center
Host: Stigg, infrastructure for the AI economy. This isn't a Stigg user conference; you don't need to use Stigg.
Building the systems behind AI usage, pricing, or billing? Request to join.

Chris Miller (Workato) — Where Do I Start? Finding Opportunities for Automation in Your Data

Prathmesh Patel (MCPJam) —  Rethinking CI/CD Release Gates for MCP servers & Agent-native Software
Human-facing software doesn't ship without a release gate: tests, type checks, linters, and security scans must all pass first. Agent-native software (MCP servers and other tools) needs different testing standards, but mostly ships without any of it.This session introduces a 4-layer automated release gate built for agent-invoked software: security, behavioral evals, protocol compliance, deterministic fast-failsWe'll show how to combine rigid hard-fails with probabilistic gates to block broken code without stalling development. Grounded in production failures, you'll leave with a concrete CI/CD checklist for safely shipping agent-facing software like MCP servers.

About this Seminar
A Decision Theorist's Journey from Theory to Decisions
For a century, theoretical ecology has used models to mimic patterns in nature: oscillations, tipping points, and the mechanisms behind them. We got good at this, and often our models fit the data almost too well. But when models are used to make decisions, a harder question arises: which model is correct? In this talk I trace a path from that question to the tools of decision theory. Stochastic dynamic programming and partially observed Markov decision processes let us find good policies under uncertainty, and they show that how we handle uncertainty can change the decision in practice. They also reveal a trap: choosing the model that forecasts best can lead us to over-exploit an ecosystem while becoming increasingly confident that we are not. No model is a crystal ball, and the future depends on what we do. I then describe how reinforcement learning, which is closely related to adaptive management, can learn policies across many candidate models, with examples from fisheries with tipping points, age-structured stocks under partial observation, and invasive green crab management. These methods carry their own risks, since an algorithm optimizes what we say we want rather than what we actually want. The same lessons apply to large language models and agentic AI, and to biodiversity data, which tells us as much about people as about the species it records. This leads to our efforts to put these lessons into practice with partners such as the Trust for Public Land, the California Department of Fish and Wildlife, BOSL and others. Working with them, we examine what can be done with small, open AI models empowered by tool use and cloud-native data workflows. Local models need no data center, sidestepping both the energy footprint and the privacy concerns of commercial AI
https://bidmap.berkeley.edu/seminars/carl-boettiger-decision-theorists-journey-theory-decisions
Our Speaker:
Carl Boettiger
Carl Boettiger is an Associate Professor in the Department of Environmental Science, Policy, and Management at the University of California, Berkeley. His research applies data science to global change biology, focusing on ecological forecasting and decision-making under uncertainty. By blending theoretical ecology with advanced computational methods, Carl develops tools to predict and manage regime shifts in vulnerable ecosystems. A leader in the open science movement, Carl is a co-founder of rOpenSci, a project that promotes software standards and reproducibility in scientific research. He also serves as a faculty affiliate at the Berkeley Institute for Data Science (BIDS) and faculty advisor to the Eric & Wendy Schmidt Center for Data Science and Environment. What makes people fall in love with a product?
Building software has never been easier. Ideas that once took months to bring to life can now be built in hours. But creating something people truly love is still incredibly hard.
As the barriers to building disappear, design becomes one of the most powerful advantages a founder can have.
Felix Haas has spent the last decade designing products and helping build companies from the ground up. At 17, he moved to Palo Alto to build his first startup. Since then, he's helped shape companies like Gorillas and Lovable, co-founded a design studio that was later acquired, and backed early-stage founders as an angel investor and Scout at Sequoia Capital.
Today, he helps lead design and brand at Lovable, where the team is making software creation accessible to everyone.
In this conversation, hosted by the Stanford GSB Entrepreneurship Club, Felix will share lessons from building Lovable and his experience working with founders, exploring how great design can turn an idea into a company people love.

From zero to one. How to approach designing your first product, what to focus on, and what to ignore.

Building a brand from scratch. A look into how Felix approaches brand strategy, identity, and creating something people remember.
The future of building. What changes when anyone can create software, and what will set the best companies apart.
Expect an open conversation, practical insights, and a look behind the scenes at Lovable.

Notebook.link: Rethinking Scientific Communication with Scalable, Interactive, AI-enabled Jupyter Notebooks
Sylvain Corlay and Jeremy Tuloup, CEO and Technical Director at Quantstack, will present Notebook.link: a new platform designed to change how scientific knowledge is shared and communicated. Drawing on over a decade of maintaining and advancing the Jupyter ecosystem, Corlay and Tuloup will describe a paradigm that goes beyond static content or traditional “Jupyter as a service” solutions. Notebook.link enables live, interactive notebooks — complete with language kernels, widgets, and custom packages — that can be shared publicly at scale and embedded directly in web articles, blogs, and presentations. They will give an overview of the current options for using AI in Jupyter, from terminal coding agents and assistants running directly in the browser to Jupyter AI’s integrated chat and notebook tools. The talk highlights how these approaches fit different workflows and environments, from JupyterLab to JupyterLite, and explore Jupyter’s impact on open science, reproducibility, and public engagement with research.

event.description:
Artwork by De’Vonne Foxworth. Curated by Tolani Verissimo. Presented by Joyce Gordon Foundation.
“OUTSIDE” is the first exhibit presentation by Bay Area artist De’Vonne Foxworth, and it’s only fitting to experience it at the pulse of fine art in downtown Oakland - Joyce Gordon Gallery.
At its heart, “OUTSIDE” explores escapism and the liberating freedom found in choosing where our minds, bodies, and spirits play. For Black youth, the choice to escape into wonder, creativity, and adventure is an intentional claim to absolute personhood. When we lean into cathartic release, we assert that our capacity for happiness, fantasy, and peace is entirely our own.
To actively choose joy in the face of life's struggles is an act of radical self-defiance. Joy functions as a spiritual disruptor—it declares that external hardships do not hold the power to dictate our internal world or limit our imagination. The body of work by De’Vonne Foxworth centers this truth: the Black experience is defined by the profound, glowing moments of freedom built through our own choices, activities, and collective refuge.
Come witness the ESCAPE. Friday November 6th. At Joyce Gordon Gallery.

Join this special ClawCamp Campfire to dive deeper into Sovereign AI, and owning more of your agentic AI Stack.
In a fast evolving agentic world where privacy is becoming harder and harder to maintain, and questions continue to rise around where your data goes and how it's being used by service providers; sovereign AI models, harnesses, and tools are evolving alongside their frontier counterparts. Join us to explore Sovereign AI options that allow you to own more of your agentic AI Stack, in order to maintain privacy and control access to your intellectual property.
This Campfire is hosted at the Luxor AI Cloud office, home of Tenki, and every attendee gets $500 in Tenki credits to run their own sandboxes (details below).
Learn more at ClawCamp.org
Want to Mentor, Speak, Sponsor, Volunteer, or Partner? Fill out our contact form: Aiify.io/form
📅 Schedule
6:00pm: Doors Open
6:30pm: Your Editor Local, Your Compute Anywhere: Crabbox + Tenki Sandboxes by Colin Lowenberg
6:45pm: Local AI Workshop by Jason Stine
7:40pm: Big Models, Little Machines: Distributed AI Workshop by Kirah Sapong
8:15pm: Scoping and Permissioning AI for a Shared Future by Rayyan Zahid
8:30pm: Networking and Wrap up
9:00pm: Doors Close
🎁 $500 in Tenki credits for every attendee
Tenki by Luxor.ai is sponsoring this Campfire with $500 in cloud credits per attendee, no credit card required.
Spend them on Sandboxes (Linux VMs your agent can run code in), GitHub Actions Runners, or Code Reviewer.
The fastest way in is to let your agent set itself up. Paste this into OpenClaw, Claude Code, Codex, or whichever harness you use:
Onboard me to Tenki. Follow the agent instructions at https://tenki.cloud/skill.md and set me up end to end.
📦 Your Editor Local, Your Compute Anywhere: Crabbox + Tenki Sandboxes by Colin Lowenberg
Running a model on your laptop keeps your prompts private. Running your agent's code on your laptop is a different problem: an agent that can run shell commands can also delete your home directory, and a laptop can only hold so many parallel jobs.
Crabbox (https://crabbox.sh), the new CLI from the OpenClaw team, solves this by keeping your editor and working tree local while running every command in the box you choose: a local container, your own SSH host, or a managed sandbox. Tenki is one of its providers, so the same crabbox run you use on your laptop can run on a fresh Linux VM in the cloud and stream the result back.
In 15 minutes, Colin will show:
crabbox run --provider tenki -- pnpm test from a local checkout, with the sandbox created, synced, run and torn down for you.
The OpenClaw Tenki sandbox backend (https://github.com/LuxorLabs/tenki-openclaw), so every tool call your OpenClaw agent makes runs in a remote VM instead of on your machine.
An OpenClaw gateway running entirely on a Tenki sandbox. Live demo at https://claw.moi
Worked examples to follow along with or try later:
Crabbox Tenki provider docs: https://crabbox.sh/providers/tenki.html
Crabbox + Tenki cookbook: https://github.com/LuxorLabs/cookbook/tree/main/examples/crabbox-tenki
OpenClaw Tenki plugin: https://github.com/LuxorLabs/tenki-openclaw
💻 Local AI Workshop by Jason Stine
Ever feel uncomfortable about sharing too much personal info with ChatGPT/Gemini/Claude but still want AI’s help? Against giving Big Tech your private life on a golden platter running on wasteful resource-sucking data centers? This workshop is for you! ​Earlier this year there was a breakthrough - we can now run AI that are more than capable of being private and even completely offline assistants on personal computers and laptops!
This is also a workshop for anyone who find setting up agents with OpenClaw too intimidating but still want a capable AI experience like ChatGPT that keeps all private information on their own computers - without writing any code or running any terminal/command line commands!
What we'll cover:
Setting up Unsloth Desktop (open source ChatGPT-like interface) and running powerful open source AI models of your choosing on your own computer.
Learning important concepts about running AI on your own computer - from why open source AI exists to tokens, context, model quantization, MCP tool servers, and more.
This is a hands-on workshop - bring your computer and get ready to download and install some AI!
System Requirements: The more RAM your computer has, the better. It’s now possible to run near-frontier-capable-AI on computers with just 16GB of RAM. That said, even if your computer has less than that (like 8GB), you can run less powerful AI that is still impressive and are welcome to attend!
To be efficient, we encourage participants to download and install Unsloth Desktop (https://unsloth.ai/docs/desktop) as well as let it automatically download a suitable AI model it selects for you (if any) when first running the app in advance before coming to the event. During the event, you’ll learn how to find even better AI models to add to your Unsloth Desktop setup.
🛠️Big Models, Little Machines: Distributed AI Workshop by Kirah Sapong
Running AI models on your own computer is exciting, but even powerful laptops have limits. By connecting multiple computers together, we can combine their resources to run larger AI models than any one device could handle alone.
In this workshop for all levels, we’ll explore distributed AI inference: how multiple computers can work together to run AI. We’ll demonstrate how to split AI models across devices using Aquaduck, without writing any code!
What we’ll cover:
Understanding how AI models run on your computer and why memory matters.
⁠Learning how multiple computers can work together to run AI.
Exploring model splitting and how it enables larger AI models to run across devices.
Getting hands-on with Aquaduck to connect computers and run AI together.
Bring your laptop and get ready to experiment with running AI across multiple devices.
You can download and install Aquaduck (https://aquaduck.ai) ahead of time so you can jump straight into the hands-on activities. No prior AI experience or programming knowledge is required.
✅ Scoping and Permissioning AI for a Shared Future by Rayyan Zahid
Rayyan will introduce some tips and strategies on properly setting the scopes and permissions for AI and agents.
💡 Sponsors & Partners
🎤 Speakers & Mentors
Colin Lowenberg: Colin works on Tenki, the cloud sandbox platform from Luxor.ai, and runs Dabl Club, a builder community in San Francisco. He spends most days putting coding agents on remote VMs and keeping them off his laptop.
Jason Stine: Jason is actually in no way related to Unsloth. He's just a passionate AI hobbyist who enjoys mentoring others and found that Unsloth Desktop was the most straightforward software for this workshop. He's a fullstack web developer (software engineer) who uses Cursor AI every day at work.
Kirah Sapong: Kirah is a co-founder at Supermodel Labs, working on AI systems. Previously, she worked on model evaluations and AI platform products at Together AI, decentralized systems and developer platforms at Block, and is currently pursuing an M.S. in Artificial Intelligence at the University of Pennsylvania. Her research interests include agent systems, inference optimization, and AI economics.

PHG Paschal-Hunter Gallery presents THE INSATIABLE QUEST FOR FEELING, an interactive art exhibit where gallery visitors are invited to collaborate with each other to build a digital archive documenting the human experience.
On a mission to understand what it means to feel, an AI agent invites gallery visitors to leave notes to future visitors with the prompt: “What does being me feel like?” As visitors leave their notes, they watch the outcome of their action unfold and they begin to weigh if contributing to this beautiful archive was worth the cost of what it unlocks.
Join for an engaging conversation with multimedia artist and Forbes’ Top 50 Women in Tech programmer Daphne Larose-Molapo around what inspired the work and how it ties in themes of spirituality, identity, AI, and humanity’s opportunity to pause and reflect on itself. Interact with the installation and decide for yourself if the ends justify the means.

TICKETS AVAILABLE AT THE DOOR: Tickets will be available for purchase at the door. Seating is limited and first come, first serve.
DISCOUNT AT THE DOOR: All teachers and students who attend this event can present an ID at the door and receive $5 off the ticket price.
ARTIST BIO: Daphne Larose-Molapo is a celebrated programmer and multimedia artist. As a programmer for nearly 20 years, Daphne has been featured as one Forbes’ Top 50 Women in Tech, holds a patent for building innovative tech in the top app store game Pokemon GO, among many other accolades. She has worked on incredible features at esteemed companies like Apple and led teams as a senior software engineer on Pokemon GO. She is currently CTO of Wicked Saints Studios, a game startup dedicated to empowering young people to build real-life skills and create real change.
As a multimedia artist, Daphne has the space to combine her skills with her sharp eye and creative lens and push the limits on the kinds of questions we ask ourselves. She believes when we push technology as a society, we should do so consciously; that we should never move so fast that we rid ourselves of the time to question and evaluate. As an artist, she sees the value of grappling with challenging big picture questions and fine art provides the perfect avenue to encourage others to do the same so that they can arrive at their own conclusions, whether that conclusion is changing directions or staying the course, full speed ahead.

Episode 02 of “Rethinking the World in the Age of AI” — a six-part series
Every era has one question it can’t stop asking.
Ours is this:
What happens when intelligence stops being scarce?
Across six sessions, this series follows that question wherever it leads — from the search box to AI agents that work alongside us, from the infrastructure powering intelligence to robots entering the physical world, from AI accelerating scientific discovery to the question that ultimately belongs to everyone:
What should we build?

From Software That Answers to Agents That Act
For decades, software has waited for humans to tell it what to do.
Open the app.Click the button.Write the prompt.Execute the task.
Generative AI changed the interface.
You could ask a question and get an answer.
But AI agents are beginning to change something deeper.
They are changing who — or what — takes the next action.
Instead of simply responding to instructions, increasingly capable AI systems can reason, plan, use tools, maintain context, coordinate across systems, and take actions toward a goal.
We are beginning to move from:
Answers → ActionsTools → CollaboratorsTasks → OutcomesSoftware → Autonomous Systems
And that shift could reshape much more than productivity.
It could change how companies are built, how teams operate, how software is designed, how organizations allocate work, and ultimately what it means to work alongside machines.
We are moving from an era where humans operate software to one where humans increasingly delegate to intelligence.
Join us at Stanford for this Special Edition of Episode 02: Rethinking Agents from Rethinking the World in the Age of AI, as we bring together builders, investors, founders, researchers, and operators to explore what happens when AI moves beyond answering questions and begins taking meaningful action in the world.
From AI-native product design and agentic workflows to the companies and interfaces emerging around autonomous systems, this session asks what changes when intelligence becomes not only available — but actionable.
AI Agents Are Still Early
Many systems remain unreliable.
Long-running tasks remain difficult.
Memory is imperfect.
Agents still struggle with ambiguity, edge cases, and environments they have never seen before.
Permissions, security, evaluation, accountability, and alignment remain open problems.
And the more agents can do, the more consequential those problems become.
But the direction is becoming increasingly clear:
AI is moving from answering questions to taking actions.
That transition could become one of the defining platform shifts of the next decade.
For builders, it raises a new question:
How do you design a product when the user is no longer responsible for every individual action?
For founders:
What businesses become possible when intelligence itself becomes a programmable resource?
For companies:
What does an organization look like when every employee can delegate work to AI agents?
For investors:
Where does durable value accrue when agents can increasingly execute workflows that once required entire layers of software and human coordination?
For researchers and product teams:
How do we build autonomous systems that remain reliable, controllable, secure, understandable, and aligned with human intent?
And for all of us:
What becomes uniquely human when machines can increasingly reason, coordinate, decide, and act?
Whether you’re building AI products, investing in frontier technologies, conducting research, operating a company, or simply curious about where AI is headed, this forum is an opportunity to hear from and connect with people thinking seriously about what comes next.
The next decade of work may not be defined by humans versus AI.
It may be defined by what we choose to delegate — and what we choose to keep human.
This Is Episode 02 — Special Edition
The story started with search.
Then intelligence began helping us create.
Now intelligence leaves the search box — and starts taking action.
Our previous Special Edition explored what happens when AI starts building alongside us.
This edition takes the next step:
What happens when AI can act, not just answer?
When AI can browse, call tools, manipulate software, coordinate workflows, write and execute code, interact with other agents, and pursue outcomes rather than simply return information, the relationship between humans and computers begins to change.
The interface is no longer just a prompt.
The product is no longer just a tool.
And the human is no longer necessarily the person executing every step.
This Special Edition goes deeper into that transition — looking at what happens when AI agents move from assisting with individual tasks toward becoming systems we can increasingly delegate real work to.
From here, we’ll follow the story deeper into the infrastructure powering these systems, into the physical world, into scientific discovery, and ultimately into the question of what we choose to build.
This is only the beginning.

THE STORY BEHIND THESE SESSIONS
I'm Sophie Ren. I build thousands of AI agents and I love watching them. Six times a year I put a few thousand people in a room together - in Silicon Valley, in Paris, in Milan, and next May at an AI × Art festival in Sicily.
I do both for the same reason. The models have already read everything we've written down. That's the floor now, not the ceiling. What I want is what isn't in there yet - the thing nobody has tried, or has tried and never said out loud. That kind of knowledge can't be collected. It gets made, and it gets made between people, in real time, in a room. That's the part I find thrilling, and I think it's where the real value has moved.
Monet painted the same pond for thirty years. At some point it stopped being a pond and became something that had never existed — not a better painting, a new object in the world. That moment and the moment a room finally cracks a problem are the same moment: the tree of human knowledge grows a branch.
Everything a model knows came from a branch that grew before it. I don't want to watch the next one grow. I want to grow it, and I want to find the people who want to grow one too.
Bring what you're stuck on.
— Sophie

event.description:
🧠 What if people with paralysis could move again?
Roughly one in fifty Americans lives with some form of paralysis, most often caused by stroke or spinal cord injury. In these cases, the pathway between brain and body has been interrupted, but the neural signals that would normally drive movement are still very much alive at the source.
Brain-computer interfaces (BCIs) offer a way around the injury. By reading signals directly from the brain and rerouting them to a device, whether a robotic arm, a computer cursor, or the person's own paralyzed limb, this technology can restore a kind of movement that was once thought to be lost.
Join Kushaal Rao, a PhD candidate in neuroscience at Brown University, as he demystifies how brain-computer interfaces actually work, where the science currently stands, and what the future might hold for people living with paralysis. ✨

event.description:
Join Crosstown Trails founder Bob Siegel on a 6-mile walk from Lands End to Presidio Tunnel Tops. Our route follows Section 5 of the new Roundabout as well as a stretch of the new Golden Gate Dozen Trail. At Land’s End, we’ll take in the views and imagine what life might have been like long ago – in the early 20th century when the Sutro Baths were in their heyday, or even farther back, when Yelamu Ohlone lived off the land. We’ll head east along the scenic Coastal Trail, following the old rail line that once brought visitors to Adolph Sutro’s oceanside attractions. We weave through the beautiful Sea Cliff neighborhood, hit the sand at famed Baker Beach, and climb the notorious Sand Ladder. We’ll be rewarded by breathtaking views of the Marin Headlands on our way to the Golden Gate Bridge. We descend to Crissy Field, a historic 1920s airfield, and finish at the main post of the Presidio, which is celebrating its 250th anniversary.
While the walk is entirely free, your optional donations to the Golden Gate National Parks Conservancy as well as the Crosstown Trails directly fund the upkeep of these stunning public spaces. Come discover how truly connected our city’s parks and neighborhoods really are.
Route Overview
The 6-mile point-to-point walk hugs San Francisco's dramatic northwestern edge. You can visit The Roundabout for self-guided exploration of the full 38-mile trail any time of the year.
Travel & Logistics
Because this is a point-to-point walk, we recommend taking public transit.
Getting to the start: Meet at Lands End Lookout Visitor Center, convenient to the Muni 38R Geary Rapid and the Muni 18 46th Ave.
Returning from the finish: The walk ends at Presidio Tunnel Tops, a major transit hub. Catch the free Presidio GO Shuttle, the Muni 43 Masonic, or the Muni 30 Stockton, all near the park's many dining options.
The fine print: Terrain is a mix of dirt trails, sand, pavement, and stairs. Bring snacks, water, layers, and anything else you need.
Co-hosted by SF Crosstown Trails and the Golden Gate National Parks Conservancy

Join us for a hands-on workshop on model customization with AWS and NVIDIA.
As companies move from AI prototypes to production, off-the-shelf models may not meet the accuracy, latency, and cost requirements. Whether it's an agent that drops tools, a chatbot that hallucinates, the model needs to learn your data, your rules, your domain. Fine-tuning a smaller open-weight model like Nemotron 3 on targeted tasks can match or exceed much larger proprietary models, delivering real cost savings while keeping your data inside your own secure infrastructure.
This workshop gives you the hands-on experience to make that happen, and you'll leave with a customized model and a follow-up plan in hand.
What You'll Learn:
Apply a customization framework to decide when to prompt-engineer vs. fine-tune
Run a supervised fine-tuning (SFT) job on Nemotron 3 using Amazon Sagemaker AI
Learn how model customization can improve agentic systems
Understand when and how to use different types of fine-tuning techniques
Evaluate your customized model against your baseline using custom metrics and benchmark evaluations
Deploy your fine-tuned model to a SageMaker real-time endpoint

event.description:
Worlds for Agents: World Models and the Agents That Learn Inside Them
A Frontier Research Club session hosted at SignalFire.
If a model can generate a world, an agent can practice in it. This session asks how far that loop actually goes.
World models promise to make agent training cheap: generate a world, let an agent act in it, score the attempt, repeat. In late 2025, DeepMind's SIMA 2 agent kept improving inside worlds generated by Genie 3, with no new human demonstrations. Whether this scales comes down to two open questions: can a generated world hold together for longer than a few minutes, and do skills learned inside one carry over to the real world?
Bonnie Li is a Research Scientist at OpenAI. At Google DeepMind, she worked on Gemini, the Genie world models and SIMA 2, and she began her research career at Mila with Yoshua Bengio.
Pre-reads go to confirmed guests the week before. Come having read them; the discussion starts at depth.
The Frontier Research Club is a curated forum for rigorous, technical discussion at the frontier of AI. We convene researchers from the frontier labs, Stanford, Berkeley and leading startups to examine concrete work (papers, methods and results) with a bias toward assumptions, evaluation methodology, failure modes, and what would count as convincing evidence.
Each session features 2 talks selected for rigor and discussion value. Presentations are intentionally brief so the majority of time is reserved for questions and critique. Papers and supporting materials are shared in advance to ensure a high-baseline conversation.
Agenda
5:30pm: Doors open5:30pm – 6:30pm: Networking + light dinner6:30pm – 8:00pm: Research presentations + discussion8:00pm – 8:30pm: Networking
Presenters & topics
Talk 1 — Bonnie Li, Research Scientist, OpenAIWorld Models as Training Grounds for Agents (working title)
Bonnie will walk through what it takes for a world model to be something an agent can learn in, not just watch: worlds that stay consistent as the agent acts, respond to what it does, and come with tasks and rewards generated alongside them. She'll close on the failure modes that matter for training, including agents that learn to exploit the simulator's errors instead of the skill.

This week's reading:
Neural Networks Are Already Clean (Nick Cammarata, Goodfire)
Link: https://already-clean.goodfire.com/
About the session:
A common view in interpretability is that neural networks are tangled knots: individual neurons do several unrelated jobs (polysemanticity), because networks cram more concepts than they have room for into shared neurons (superposition). If that is right, you cannot study neurons directly and need tools like sparse autoencoders to unfold the network first.
This essay argues the opposite. It revisits classic examples such as the InceptionV1 "cat and car" neuron and re-reads them as ordinary features like V-shape and pose detectors. It then looks at vision models of very different sizes and at language-model neurons in Qwen3-32B. The author's claim is that most apparent polysemanticity comes from fixable causes (weak visualization tools, missing architecture features, thin datasets) and from neurons growing in several directions over training, not from superposition.
Thomas will walk through the post, then step back and cover some wider AI interpretability concepts at a high level, so you do not need a background in the field.
Relevant to anyone curious about how models work inside, from newcomers to interpretability to people who have used SAEs. No preparation required. Come read and discuss with us.
Thomas will lead the discussion this week.
What is the Learning Layer Labs Paper Reading Club?
An initiative from https://www.learninglayer.ai, a lab with the goal of reducing AI anxiety in the world.
What is the format?
Discussion based. Expect a low pressure environment to share insights and opinions with the group.
What are the group goals?
Stay on top of AI research and improve understanding of AI fundamentals + math.
Who is welcome?
Everyone! Try to put in at least some time on the paper and come prepared with questions or things you'd like to discuss, but it's ok to just show up!

Mat Allen (The new fella bring order and organization)

Build a Sovereign AI Model Factory: an ML Engineer Agent that evaluates, fine-tunes, deploys, and improves open models using Union on your cloud.
The best AI teams aren't renting every capability from an external API, they're building systems they own and control. In this hands-on session at the AWS Loft, we'll build exactly that.
We'll start with a walkthrough where we build a LangGraph-powered agent that evaluates open models in parallel, fine-tunes promising candidates, deploys the winner, and retrains automatically when performance drops. Think of it as the first brick in your own model factory: a repeatable system for evaluating, improving, and deploying models you control, not a black box you call and hope for the best.
Along the way, you'll see how Union.ai gives your workflows a durable runtime with infrastructure as context, so agents adapt infra resources, recover from failures, and keep moving without re-running completed work. And because it all runs in your own AWS account, you own the full stack end to end: your models, your data, your infrastructure, your IP.
Then we switch into hack night mode: keep building on the example, bring your own models or datasets, experiment with evals and fine-tuning, extend open models to different parts of your agent, or start something new around the same ideas.
For teams thinking about sovereign AI, this is a practical starting point for owning more of your stack, the weights, the training loop, the evals, and the infrastructure it runs on, all on AWS.

event.description:
Join Liquid AI and the San Francisco AI community for an evening dedicated to decision models: purpose-built models that make fast, structured decisions without generating tokens.
Unlike language models that produce free-form text, decision models return calibrated probabilities for outcomes such as:
Noul: Should this action happen?
Choice: Which option should the system select?
Score: How should this input be rated?
Not every AI task needs generation. Routing requests, approving agent actions, moderating content, evaluating outputs and inspecting images often require a clear, reliable decision, not another paragraph of text.
Decision models offer a new way to build these systems: predictable structured outputs, calibrated confidence, low latency and zero generated tokens. They can work independently or alongside LLMs as fast decision layers for agents and production applications.
Come learn how they work, explore where they fit in the modern AI stack and see what developers are already building with Liquid's decision model family across text, vision and audio.

Help me test-drive my first Hackaday Supercon workshop!
I'm running my first-ever workshop at Hackaday Supercon this year. It's the "exquisite corpse" drawing game, but for electronics, and I'd love to do a trial run with friendly local faces first. Come be my workshop guinea pigs!
Here's how it will work: Everyone gets a small synth module and modifies it in secret. Then we chain all the blocks together, power them up, and find out whether our collective creation plays a tune you'll recognize. Think Lego Great Ball Contraption, but for sound, with lots more ways to go gloriously wrong.
No experience needed. I'll ask for your feedback at the end, so you'll get to help shape the real thing. I will bring snacks & drinks. Come help me make it awesome?
It would mean a lot to have you there!
Workshop descriptions are online at: https://hackaday.com/2026/10/14/2026-hackaday-supercon-workshops-are-open/
My workshop description is below:
Exquisite Circuit: Exquisite Corpse for Electronics
What happens when a circuit is designed by a room full of people who cannot see the whole circuit?
In this hands-on electronic version of Exquisite Corpse, each participant adds a stage to a shared low-voltage circuit, conceals their work, and passes it to the next builder. Participants inherit standardized power and signal connections – but no schematic, explanation, or design review.
At the end, we reveal the complete creations, attempt to reconstruct their collective logic, inspect them for safety, and apply power from a strictly current-limited supply. Functionality is optional. Surprise is guaranteed.
event.title: Exquisite Circuit: a Hackaday Supercon workshop test-drive with Alessandra

event.description:
A live 60-minute training where you build the internal tool you have been postponing — scope, build, deploy — and put it at a live URL before you leave the room.
Everyone has one. The small internal thing that would save four hours a week and has never been built, because it would take an engineer two days and the engineer has a roadmap. So it stays on the list, quietly costing you four hours a week, forever. That calculation just changed, and most people have not noticed yet.
In this session, Arjita Sethi, founder of Build with AI Club, builds a working internal tool from scratch in front of you, deploys it, and hands you the method. You bring the thing that has been on your list longest.
What you will learn:
How to scope a tool small enough to actually finish in one sitting
Describing what you want in a way that produces working software rather than a broken draft
Building and testing it live, watching what breaks and why
Deploying to a real URL you can send to someone else
When to build it yourself, and when a tool is the wrong answer to the problem
What you will walk away with:
One working tool, deployed, at a URL you can share today
The method, repeatable for the next four things on your list
A different sense of what counts as too small to build
Who this is for: The internal dashboard, the intake form, the calculator, the tracker, the thing you currently do in a spreadsheet at 11pm. Bring it. No technical background required, and no code will be written by hand.
Joining virtually? Here's what to expect.
Virtual seats are an audit pass. You're dropping into a live, in-person session with Arjita at SHACK15 and watching her build in real time. The session is run for the people in the room, so virtual attendees won't be able to ask questions or get hands-on help during the session. Come to watch, take notes and build along at your own pace.
Want to build with Arjita live and get your questions answered? That's exactly what Build with AI Club is for. This session is a standalone free event and is not part of a paid program. See the full programs: AI for Growth and AI for Ops.
Your host: Arjita Sethi is the founder of Build with AI Club, creator of the vibe-coded wellness platform Find Shaanti, a Lecturer of Entrepreneurship at San Francisco State University, Advisory Board member at the Nasdaq Entrepreneurial Center, and a Claude Community Ambassador for San Francisco for the non-technical and moms vertical. She has built three companies without writing a line of code by hand.

About your host: Dylan Zhang is the founder and CEO of Pond AI. As a solo founder, he has raised a $7.5M seed round and attracted 30+ heavyweight angel investors.
A personal note from Dylan:
I've always felt like a misfit. I don't go to parties very often, and I spend most of my time alone, reading, thinking and building. I'm a founder, but I've also studied art, philosophy, and engineering. I've always been drawn to deep conversations, exchanging ideas, and supporting others.
I want to create a peaceful spot in San Francisco where like-minded people can meet, make friends, discuss ideas, demo products, and exchange feedback. Hopefully, this can become something like the Homebrew Computer Club, where Steve Jobs and Steve Wozniak connected with other curious minds.

Agents are shipping code, yet humans still own the consequences. Learn from Engineering leaders across industries on what happens when agents operate in production and the stakes include real customers, sensitive data, and systems you can’t afford to break.
Join Enrich, Optimal AI and Auth0 for dinner, drinks, and a candid conversation about what it takes to put agents to work and trust its results.
We’ll dig into the decisions teams face once agents move beyond experimentation: where autonomy earns its place, where human oversight remains essential, and which pitfalls only become visible in production.
With leaders spanning fintech, robotics, security and SaaS the conversation will explore:
What breaks after deployment: Unexpected failure modes, integration challenges, and the hidden work of keeping agents reliable.
How much control to give up: Permissions, guardrails, human approvals, and knowing when to intervene.
What changes in regulated industries: Balancing speed with security, auditability, and accountability.
The new engineering playbook: How teams rethink code review, ownership, and productivity when agents become contributors.

As code multiplies in volume by 50x, organizations are facing a multitude of new problems related to quality, review and security. Customers include Bear Robotics, Forward Finance, MongoDB and many more.

event.description:
Build something that could change how the world’s best skiers and snowboarders train.
Join Cloudflare and U.S. Ski & Snowboard in San Francisco on November 9 for the launch party of a new winter sports technical challenge for builders.
Cloudflare and U.S. Ski & Snowboard are teaming up to invite developers to build tools using real ski and snowboard footage/data. The goal is to explore how AI, computer vision, video analysis, and Cloudflare’s developer platform can help athletes and coaches turn competition footage into useful training insights.
At the launch party, we’ll introduce the challenge, walk through the two technical tracks, explain the available footage/data, and share how participants can build and submit projects on Cloudflare.
The Challenges - STARTER PACK
Participants can choose one challenge track or build for both. Each track includes real competition footage/data, sport-specific context, technical guidance, and example outputs to help builders understand the problem space.
Challenge 1: Snowboard Rotation Analysis 🏂
Can you teach a computer to understand a snowboard trick?
When a snowboarder launches into the air, coaches can see the trick, but measuring exactly how the rider rotates throughout the jump is much harder.
Your challenge is to build a video-analysis tool that tracks a snowboarder’s rotation during aerial tricks. Using real slopestyle and halfpipe footage, participants can identify takeoff and landing, estimate rotation angles and speed, and visualize how a rider moves through the air.
The goal is to give coaches and athletes a better way to understand what happens during a trick.
🏆 Prize: Two VIP tickets to the Toyota U.S. Grand Prix at Aspen Snowmass, February 27–28, 2027. Includes lift tickets and gift bags.
Snowboard Starter Pack: Footage, technical guidance, example outputs, and judging criteria.
Challenge 2: Alpine Race Telemetry ⛷️
Can you show exactly where a ski race was won or lost?
In Alpine skiing, races can be decided by hundredths of a second. But knowing who finished fastest does not tell coaches where an athlete gained or lost time.
Your challenge is to build a tool that turns real race footage into a live performance breakdown. Using Super-G and Downhill footage, participants can create video overlays showing estimated speed, elapsed time, and where a skier is gaining or losing time compared to another run.
Think of it as building a live analytics dashboard directly on top of ski race footage.
🏆 Prize: Two VIP tickets to the FIS Ski World Cup Finals in Sun Valley, March 20–21, 2027. Includes lift tickets and gift bags
Alpine Telemetry Starter Pack: Race footage, sample data, technical guidance, example outputs, and judging criteria.
How It Works
1. Join the launch party. Learn about the challenge, the available footage/data, the two technical tracks, and what a successful prototype could look like.
2. Pick your challenge. Choose Snowboard Rotation Analysis, Alpine Race Telemetry, or both.
3. Build and deploy on Cloudflare. Create a working prototype using whichever Cloudflare tools make sense for your project. You can use Workers, Pages, R2, Workers AI, AI Gateway, or other Cloudflare developer products.
4. Submit your project by November 30. Share your GitHub repository, a link to your deployed prototype, and a short explanation of what you built.
You do not need to be a skiing or snowboarding expert to participate. We’ve put together starter packs to help you understand the sports, the footage, and what a useful prototype could look like.
Important Dates
November 9, 5–8 PM PT: Challenge launch party in San Francisco
November 30: Project submissions due
Winners will be selected after submissions are reviewed.
The Launch Party
We’re bringing together developers, Cloudflare, and U.S. Ski & Snowboard for a launch party in San Francisco.
Attendees will learn about the challenge, the real footage/data available to builders, the athlete and coaching problems behind each track, and how to participate.
Space is limited, so please RSVP if you plan to attend.
Challenge winners will receive VIP tickets to marquee ski and snowboard events this coming winter, consolation winners will compete for a combined $80K in Cloudflare credits.

Join us on November 10 at the Mind the Bridge Innovation Center in San Francisco for the 2026 edition of the Terna Innovation Zone Forum.
Terna, Italy's electricity Transmission System Operator, in collaboration with Mind the Bridge, brings together leading players from the European and US energy, technology and innovation ecosystems to discuss how AI, digitalization and the rapid growth of data centers are reshaping the electricity system.
The Forum will bring together grid operators and utilities, technology companies, research organizations, startups, scaleups and innovation leaders to explore how electricity grids can evolve to meet these emerging challenges.
The conversation will move from the investment and infrastructure race behind the AI economy to the challenges of connecting new large loads, unlocking more capacity from existing grids and bringing innovative GridTech solutions into real-world applications.

AI is changing how we learn, make decisions, and navigate everyday life. How do we make the most of its possibilities while staying thoughtful about its risks?
Join The AI Collective’s Tri-Valley chapter for an evening of conversation about what AI means for us today and the future we’re helping shape.
Bringing together perspectives from technology, education, and youth advocacy, we’ll explore:
How AI is influencing human decision-making, learning, and creativity
Concerns around misinformation, privacy, overreliance, and critical thinking
How parents and schools can help students develop AI literacy and use these tools responsibly
The opportunities and challenges facing the next generation
Featured speakers
Rana Gujral is an AI entrepreneur, operator, and author of The AI Instinct (Wiley, 2026), with a foreword by Kai-Fu Lee. He is the former CEO of Behavioral Signals, an In-Q-Tel backed company building emotion and behavior AI from voice, and currently leads Renu Ventures. He serves on the board of Cartica Acquisition Corp and advises TNW and the Global AI Council. His career spans product and platform leadership at Logitech, Cricut, and Kronos. A TEDx speaker, he writes and speaks on how humans and AI will evolve together. He lives in Danville.
Amy Gao is a sophomore at Emerald High School (Dublin, CA) and the founder and president of Girls in AI, a student club dedicated to empowering girls through AI. An award-winning young innovator, Amy received the Bronze Award at AI YES 2026, third place at the Alameda County Science and Engineering Fair and more. Amy also serves as President of the Green Apple Education Foundation, which hosted 9 years of the San Ramon hackathon. A recipient of the Congressional Award Silver Medal, an AIME qualifier, and a College Board AP Scholar in freshman year, she is passionate about making AI more accessible to young people and bringing a student perspective to conversations about AI's opportunities, risks, and future impact.
Nikhil Gujral is a youth advocate, TEDx and international speaker, and youth ambassador for the AI Collective and iRAISE, where he works on AI literacy, ethical AI, and AI regulation from a next-generation perspective. He has spoken at UNESCO House in Paris and the French Consulate in San Francisco, engaging diplomats and researchers on youth voice in AI policy. A nationally ranked debater on the USA Debate Development Team, his 2025 TEDx talk, The Forgotten Joy of Hobbies, makes the case for creativity and play in a culture obsessed with output. He is a student at Monte Vista High School.
Moderator
Saba Assadi Handjani is the founder of Lumino Learning AI, a company built on a simple belief: AI should help learners stay curious and think for themselves, not do their thinking for them. A Waldorf school alum, Saba brings that tradition's focus on creativity, independent thought and the whole learner into the age of AI. Through Lumino and its AI Education Academy, an after-school program for high school students, she's preparing young people to grow alongside AI, face real challenges, and make good choices in an AI-shaped future.
Attendees
This event is open to parents, educators, community members, and anyone curious about AI’s impact. High school students are encouraged to join, and younger students are welcome with their parents. No technical background needed, just curiosity and questions.

7:15–7:40 p.m. — Audience Q&A
7:40 — Closing talk by Melissa West, Assistant Principal at Emerald high school

We appreciate your application tremendously and we are looking forward to seeing you at a future event very soon!

event.description:
Is Deployment the Real Moat in Physical AI?
What does it really take to deploy robots at scale, and can deployment become a lasting competitive advantage?
As robotics foundation models and hardware continue to advance, real-world deployment remains one of the industry's biggest challenges.
What separates a successful demo from a scalable business? Is the real moat in the technology, the deployment expertise, the operational data, or the customer relationships built along the way?
Join Embodied Collective for an intimate, curated industry conversation bringing together robotics companies, deployment practitioners, and enterprise adopters to exchange firsthand insights and explore what it takes to scale Physical AI in the real world.
What We'll Explore
The Deployment Bottleneck: What's actually preventing robots from scaling beyond pilots?
The Enterprise Perspective: What do industrial buyers really need before deploying robotics solutions?
Deployment as a Moat: Can real-world experience, data, and operational capabilities create sustainable competitive advantages?
Scaling in Practice: What does it take to make robotics deployments repeatable, reliable, and commercially viable?
Confirmed Speakers
Robert Scoble | Founder, Unaligned (Opening Fireside)
Robert has spent decades on the front lines of tech, from Microsoft to eight books about the future. He now tracks AI and robotics daily at Unaligned and AlignedNews.com, and visits the teams building them, giving him a rare view of what's actually running in the real world versus what's still a demo.
Ruslan Bekbulatov | Investment Principal, Bosch Ventures
Ruslan brings a unique perspective at the intersection of industrial customers and venture investing, engaging with both sides on technology capabilities, technical specifications, deployment timelines, and commercial considerations. (Views expressed are his own and do not represent Bosch or Bosch Ventures.)
Saman Farid | Founder & CEO, Formic
Saman runs Formic, which puts robots to work in American factories, and has an active and growing fleet deployed in 150 factories. In bringing Physical AI to the real world, his team has built infrastructure and software to handle deployment, monitoring and maintenance so manufacturers can automate without large upfront costs. Before Formic, he was a Partner at Baidu Ventures, leading investments in AI companies transforming traditional industries, and he founded Robots for America to advance U.S. robotics deployment policy.
Evan Tao | Co-founder & CEO, Chestnut Robotics
Formerly a core member of Tesla's Optimus team, Evan brings extensive robotics hardware experience from Tesla, Apple, and ASML. At Chestnut Robotics, he is advancing dexterous manipulation through hardware and human demonstration co-design, focusing on making robotic systems more reliable, scalable, and deployment-ready.
Natalia Kokoromyti | Co-founder & CEO, Cybernetic Physics
A Stanford computer scientist, Natalia previously worked as a researcher in Stanford’s Scaling Intelligence Lab, where she contributed to KernelBench, and worked on confidential computing at Lucid Computing. At Cybernetic Physics, an a16z speedrun company, she is building an intelligence lab for real-world machines. The company owns the hard part of putting robots to work, from bridging sim-to-real gaps and integrating robots on-site to policy serving, teleoperation, and ongoing operations, so autonomous systems can run reliably on real floors.
Judah Longgrear | Co-Founder and President of Media, Robot.com
Judah leads Robot.com's media business, R-Ads, building a first-of-its-kind robotic media network from the company's global fleet and digital out-of-home network. Robot.com is a Physical AI platform deploying autonomous robots across delivery, logistics, advertising, and security. A serial entrepreneur, Judah has spent nearly a decade building at the intersection of mobility, adtech, and robotics.
Rajesh Senthil Kumar | Head of Product and Deployment, RLWRLD
Rajesh leads product and deployment at RLWRLD, a Physical AI company developing RLDX-1, a dexterity-first robotics foundation model designed to enable human-like manipulation. By combining real-world industrial data with advanced robot learning, RLWRLD is tackling complex manipulation tasks across manufacturing, logistics, and service environments. Rajesh brings a practical perspective on bridging foundation model capabilities with real-world deployment and commercialization.
More robotics foundation model and deployment speakers to be announced!
Who Should Join?
We're especially looking to connect with:
Robotics Deployment Companies: Founders and operators building and deploying robotics solutions in real-world environments.
Enterprise Buyers & Adopters: Manufacturing, logistics, industrial, and other organizations actively deploying, piloting, or evaluating robotics technologies.
System Integrators & Deployment Partners: Teams working directly on robotics integration, implementation, and operations.
Our goal is to bring the people building and deploying robotics together with the businesses adopting them — creating a focused, high-signal conversation around real challenges, practical insights, and potential collaborations.

6:30 – 6:40 PM | Welcome from Embodied Collective
6:40 – 6:50 PM | Opening Fireside: What's Actually Running, and What's Still a Demo, with Robert Scoble (Unaligned)
6:50 – 7:35 PM | Panel 1 · Who Owns the Moat? Deployment as Competitive Advantage, with Ruslan Bekbulatov (Bosch Ventures), Judah Longgrear (Robot.com) and Saman Farid (Formic)

event.description:
Did Jesus Christ actually rise from the dead?
To most of us in the modern world, the question is almost so ridiculous that it's not even worth asking. Sure, Jesus may have had a few insightful moral teachings. It may even be the case that some find comfort and guidance from faith in Jesus. But to say that a 33 year old man from the backwaters of Galilee in the first century AD literally died, was buried, and miraculously came back to life is, at the very least, a bit ridiculous.
In this talk, Aditya Prathap will be making the case for why the resurrection of Jesus Christ is not only not ridiculous, but is in fact the only rational explanation of the objective historical data.
The talk will cover what is known as the Minimal Facts Argument. Concepts and sources that will be discussed include but are not limited to the following:
What Tacitus' comments on Christ in Annals (116 AD) tells us about the crucifixion of Christ.
What records of early Christian persecution from Suetonius (112 AD) and Pliny the Younger (121 AD) and the creed cited by the Apostle Paul in his letter to the Corinthians (54 AD) reveal about the sociopolitical landscape surrounding early Christians and its corresponding incentive structure.
Analysis of the medical literature relevant to common natural explanations of the historical data, including grief-induced hallucinations, mass hallucinations, and the symptoms of asphyxiation, the primary mechanism of death in Roman crucifixion.
Scholarly frameworks used to identify the reliability of data, e.g., the criterion of embarrassment.
People of any religious background or lack thereof are welcome to join. Skepticism and pushback are encouraged. No background in history or theology is needed. The talk will last ~45 minutes, followed by Q&A.
Aditya is a Christian living in San Francisco. Raised Hindu, he became an atheist after growing disillusioned with organized religion. After over a year of investigating the historical evidence for Christianity to prove that it had no rational justification, Aditya became convinced of the historicity of the resurrection of Jesus and was baptized in 2019.
event.title: The Historical Case for the Resurrection of Christ

Join BASES for a talk with Neil Movva, co-founder and CEO of Sail Research, the inference platform for long-horizon AI agents. Sail is built for agents that work on a single task for hours or days: an inference stack rebuilt around throughput and efficiency. It powers teams like Parallel, Exa, Instinct, and has raised $80M from Kleiner Perkins and Sequoia, alongside John Hennessy and Lip-Bu Tan.

Thank you for your interest!
Follow Eau Yeah! for updates on future events. We’d love to see you at the next one!
What makes a perfume smell expensive? Why do some scents disappear in minutes while others linger all day? And what happens when you mix something floral, woody, smoky, or sweet?
Join us for an hands-on perfume making workshop where we’ll explore the art and science of scent, then experiment with creating a fragrance that's entirely your own.
No perfume knowledge (or chemistry!) needed. Come curious, experiment, and meet some new people along the way. You're very welcome to come solo.
What We'll Do
This is a casual, beginner-friendly creative workshop focused on experimentation and having fun with fragrance.
Learn the Science of ScentDiscover what makes perfumes tick: fragrance notes, top/heart/base structure, why some scents last longer than others, and what makes certain combinations work.
Explore a Palette of FragrancesSmell your way through a curated collection of citrus, floral, fruity, woody, musky, gourmand, and more unusual notes. Find out what you're drawn to.
Design Your PerfumeChoose a direction and start experimenting. Maybe you're making something warm and woody, bright and fresh, dark and smoky (or something we don't have a name for yet).
Blend, Test & IterateMix a first version, smell how the notes interact, compare creations with other guests, and tweak your formula until it feels like yours.
Bottle Your CreationGive your fragrance a name, bottle your final formula, and take it home with you!
What You'll Leave With:
Your own custom 10ml bottle of perfume and your personal fragrance formula.
An beginner's understanding of how perfumes are constructed.

Join us Tuesday, November 3rd at 5:30 PM for an evening with Stefanie Hutka, design leader and author of What Your Machines Should Do: The Science and Strategy of Human-Centered Automation. Stefanie has spent her career asking a question that sounds simple until you try to answer it: what should automation actually do, and for whom?
Her talk centers on what she calls the "Automation Strategy Gap," the yawning distance between an organization's AI ambitions and its actual readiness to do something useful with them. It is, she argues, alarmingly wide. Drawing on human factors, cognitive science, and management theory, her book makes the case that AI is the latest chapter in a long history of automation, and that the durable lessons were always there, we just got distracted by the hype. One particularly useful provocation: automation accelerates the system you already have. Which means the first thing worth mapping is the beliefs driving your organization before you automate anything at all.
This is a book launch talk. Join a curated group of investors for an evening of conversation, networking, and dinner to discuss:
Can safer, sustainable battery chemistry compete at commercial scale?
Carlo Charles, founder and CEO of Flint, will join us to discuss the company he’s building and the opportunity he sees across consumer electronics, smart labels, IoT, wearables, and other emerging technologies.
Flint is developing cellulose-based batteries designed to provide a safer, non-toxic, and lower-carbon alternative to conventional battery chemistries. Its technology is intended to address applications where safety, sustainability, flexibility, and form factor are increasingly important.
View Flint’s investor deck
Rather than treating battery innovation solely as a performance problem, Flint is focused on some of the constraints that increasingly determine where and how batteries can be deployed: toxicity, safety, sustainability, form factor, manufacturing, and end-of-life considerations. The company is working with global companies and manufacturing partners as it moves from R&D toward commercialization and scalable production.
We’ll use Flint as the starting point for a broader conversation about battery technology, sustainable materials, commercialization of deep technology, and where emerging battery chemistries could create new market opportunities.
Expect a candid fireside discussion + Q&A followed by dinner and open networking. The evening is intentionally designed to leave plenty of time to circulate, meet other guests, and continue conversations independently.

Physical AI Founder × Funder: San Francisco
Beyond the Demo: Building and Funding Physical AIAutonomy · Real-World Deployment · Commercialization · Venture Capital
Presented by House of 434
http://thefoundersfunders.com/
About the Event
A Physical AI system that works in a demo is impressive. Building one that works reliably in the real world is an entirely different challenge.
As AI moves beyond screens into machines, factories, vehicles, laboratories, and other physical environments, a new generation of founders is building intelligent systems that can perceive, learn, decide, and act.
But turning these breakthroughs into successful companies comes with unique challenges. How do founders build defensible technology? What does it take to move from research and prototypes into real-world deployments? And what makes a Physical AI company attractive to investors?
Following our Founder × Funder gatherings in New York City, we’re bringing the series to San Francisco.
Physical AI Founder × Funder brings together technical founders, active investors, robotics researchers, and industry leaders for an evening exploring the opportunities and challenges of building and funding Physical AI companies.
Expect a candid founder-investor panel, five selected startup pitches, and dedicated time for meaningful introductions between people building and backing the next generation of Physical AI.
Physical AI Founder × Funder brings together technical founders, active investors, researchers, and industry leaders for an evening focused on the technologies and companies shaping the future of Physical AI.
After our New York editions, we're bringing the series to San Francisco.______________________________________________________________
What We're Exploring
World Models & Physical Simulation
AI systems that learn how physical environments behave, predict future states, and simulate outcomes. From learned world models and digital twins to physics-based AI and sim-to-real transfer.
Perception & Physical Data
Autonomy & Embodied Intelligence
How do machines learn to perceive, reason, and act in complex physical environments? From robot learning and intelligent control to autonomous planning and adaptive systems.
From Simulation to Real-World Deployment
What does it take to move beyond controlled demonstrations and build intelligent systems that operate reliably in unpredictable environments?
Perception, Physical Data & Continuous Learning
How proprietary physical data, sensor fusion, perception systems, and real-world feedback loops improve autonomous systems and create defensible advantages.
Physical AI Infrastructure
The software and infrastructure required to train, evaluate, deploy, monitor, and improve Physical AI systems, including edge intelligence, reliability, and execution platforms.
Commercialization & Venture Capital
What does it take to turn a technical breakthrough into a venture-scale business? We’ll explore customer adoption, pilot programs, deployment economics, technical differentiation, and what investors look for at the earliest stages.______________________________________________________________
Who Should Attend?
Founders Building Physical AI
We’re particularly interested in technical founders building:
Autonomous systems and embodied intelligence
Robotics software and intelligent control
Perception, spatial intelligence, and sensor fusion
Physical data infrastructure and continuous learning
Simulation-to-real-world technologies
Edge intelligence and real-time autonomy
Robotics deployment, evaluation, and reliability infrastructure
Industrial autonomy and intelligent automation
Enabling software and infrastructure for Physical AI
Whether you’re coming out of a research lab, developing a prototype, running early pilots, or preparing to raise capital, we’d love to learn what you’re building.
We’re especially interested in pre-seed and seed-stage founders with deep technical expertise, differentiated technology, and a clear vision for commercial applications.
Investors & Funders
We’re inviting active angels, venture capital firms, specialist Physical AI investors, deep-tech funds, corporate venture teams, and family offices interested in backing technical founders.
Particularly relevant are investors focused on robotics, embodied intelligence, autonomous systems, AI infrastructure, industrial technology, and frontier technologies.
Researchers & Industry Leaders
We also welcome select robotics researchers, AI engineers, technical executives, and industry operators working across autonomous systems, manufacturing, logistics, agriculture, industrial technology, and physical infrastructure.
______________________________________________________________The Founder × Funder Panel
Beyond the Demo: Building and Funding Physical AI
What separates an impressive technology demonstration from an intelligent system that can operate reliably in the real world, and a company investors want to back?
We’re bringing together experienced founders, technical leaders, and investors for a candid discussion about the journey from breakthrough technology to commercial deployment and venture investment.
We’ll explore:
Where are the biggest opportunities in Physical AI beyond the hype?
What are the hardest challenges in moving autonomous systems from research to real-world deployment?
What creates lasting defensibility: proprietary data, intelligent models, software infrastructure, or deployment experience?
Should founders build full-stack robotics businesses or focus on the intelligence and infrastructure layers?
What technical and commercial milestones make a Physical AI startup fundable at pre-seed and seed?
Where would experienced founders and investors place their bets today?

Dr. Subhash ChallaFounder, CEO,  SenSen AI | Honorary Professor, University of Melbourne
Praveen PenmetsaFounder, CEO, Motivo Engineering and Monarch

Padma Malladi -  Fractional CTO at Craftweb______________________________________________________________Five Founders Pitch LiveFive selected early-stage Physical AI companies will take the stage to present their technology and business to investors and experienced technology leaders.
